name: Wageningen University & Research
summary: Life-sciences university in the small town of Wageningen; 8 English-taught BSc programmes in food, animals, environment, oceans, data and tourism.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma. Strictest: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL plus Chemistry and Physics, one at HL (2026 list). IB taught only in English, English A at 5, or English B HL 6/SL 7 covers English.

apply.via: Studielink, then WUR's Osiris application portal

programmes.name: Animal Sciences
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, Chemistry and Biology; one of these at HL (2026 list).
programmes.about: The biology of animals, from pets to livestock and fish, and how their health, behaviour and welfare connect with people, food production and the environment, including sustainable livestock farming.
programmes.overview: Year one covers animal biology, the diversity of domesticated animals, chemistry, mathematics and statistics, and includes an internship. Year two brings genetics, ecology, immunology, zoology, animal nutrition and epidemiology, and you choose between Animal Management and Care, which looks at animals and their effects on environment and society, and Biological Functioning of Animals, which looks at internal processes. Teaching mixes lectures, group tutorials, lab and computer practicals, excursions and fieldwork. Year three offers electives and a minor, possibly abroad, and an original research thesis. Graduates work as policy advisers, researchers, teachers and animal welfare inspectors, often after a master's in animal sciences.

needs.note: One of Maths, Chemistry and Biology must be HL.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply early and send your marks so WUR can list any missing subjects. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Data Science for Global Challenges
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, plus Chemistry, Biology or Physics (2026 list). Choose the English track; a Dutch track runs alongside.
programmes.about: Data science and AI applied to climate change, health and food security, such as spotting deforestation in satellite images or tracking how diseases spread. Choose the English track.
programmes.overview: Year one combines life sciences, mathematics, statistics and computer science, and applies data science to global challenges. Year two moves to advanced data science and artificial intelligence techniques, with an emphasis on using them responsibly. You learn programming, statistical analysis and model building, and work with diverse data including satellite and sensor data, in group work that builds interdisciplinary collaboration. In year three you take electives or a minor, at one of nearly 50 options or another university, and finish with a capstone project applying data science to a global challenge. Graduates work as data scientists, AI and geo-data specialists, or epidemiologists.

programmes.name: Earth System Sciences
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, Chemistry and Physics, one of the two at HL (2026 list).
programmes.about: How soil, water and atmosphere interact, from groundwater flow to atmospheric turbulence, learned through fieldwork, lab work, simulations and data analysis, applied to floods, drought and climate. Formerly Soil, Water, Atmosphere.
programmes.overview: Year one covers the core theories of the Earth system, from processes underground to the atmosphere, with fieldwork and lab experience. Year two turns to landscape formation, water quality, weather and climate, and environmental and climate modelling, with field excursions. Teaching mixes lectures, practicals, outdoor measurements, lab experiments, data analysis and computer simulation. In year three you take a minor in the Netherlands or abroad, such as Disaster and Risk Resilience, then deepen one domain, soil, water or atmosphere, or all three, in an individual research project. Graduates work as climate researchers, water managers and environmental advisors, for example at KNMI or Deltares.

programmes.name: Environmental Sciences
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, Chemistry and Physics, one of the two at HL (2026 list).
programmes.about: The relationship between people and the environment studied through natural, social and technological sciences together, in international teams working on climate and sustainability problems.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, statistics and chemistry together with soil processes, water systems and environmental technology, applied to real sustainability challenges. In year two you prepare for and then choose a specialisation: technological, social or systems-oriented environmental science. Teaching includes lectures, group work, lab practicals, computer simulations and fieldwork, with more support staff than is typical at Dutch universities. In year three you complete your specialisation, take electives or a self-designed set of courses, and a minor such as geo-information or ecosystem governance, and finish with an independent research thesis. Graduates work as environmental researchers, policy advisers and sustainability managers.

programmes.name: Food Technology
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, Chemistry, and Biology or Physics; one of the sciences at HL (2026 list).
programmes.about: The science of making food: ingredients, processing, packaging, safety and quality, applied straight away to real products, with room to deepen or broaden as you find your interests.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, chemistry, biology, physics, microbiology and toxicology, and an introduction to food technology with excursions. Year two applies these to food microbiology, chemistry, preservation, engineering, food hazards, packaging design and quality systems, and you develop your own food product. Teaching uses lectures, tutorials, project-based learning and practicals. In year three you have free electives, case studies on real industry problems and an independent graduation thesis, with minors such as Foods of Animal Origin, an internship or study abroad. Graduates work as product developers, R&D specialists and quality managers at companies like Unilever and Heineken.

programmes.name: International Land and Water Management
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, and Physics SL or HL (2026 list).
programmes.about: Drought, erosion and flooding tackled with natural science, social science and engineering, with cases from Peru to Thailand and a third-year internship and research project abroad.
programmes.overview: Year one covers soil and water, agronomy, sociology, economics and hydraulics, with a case study and fieldwork in the Netherlands. Year two looks at the engineering, socio-economic and policy sides of land and water management, with an excursion to southern Europe to study irrigation and erosion control. Teaching uses lectures, tutorials, computer-based learning and fieldwork, with small-group work on real cases. In year three you do a practical internship abroad, take electives or a minor such as Climate Change, GIS or Education, and write a final research thesis. Graduates work as consultants, project managers and policy officers.

programmes.name: Marine Sciences
programmes.ib: Maths AI HL or AA SL/HL, Chemistry and Biology, one of the two at HL (2026 list).
programmes.about: The sea seen from nature, food and society: marine ecology alongside the ocean as a resource for the people who depend on it, working with engineers, biologists and policymakers.
programmes.overview: Year one analyses diverse marine systems and teaches research methods across disciplines, ending in fieldwork on the Wadden Sea and North Sea. Year two focuses on nature-inspired solutions to international challenges, including the responsible use of generative AI, and you present findings to industry professionals. Teaching combines lectures, group projects, lab and computer practicals and excursions to marine research institutes and coastal sites such as Texel and Croatia. In year three an elective semester allows a minor, for example Seagriculture, followed by a final project with graduation research on nature-based solutions. Graduates work as marine researchers and fisheries or aquaculture managers.

programmes.name: Tourism (joint degree)
programmes.ib: Maths AI or AA, SL or HL (2026 list). Joint degree with Breda University of Applied Sciences; you apply to WUR in Studielink.
programmes.about: Tourism studied through social, economic and environmental science, asking how travel can become more sustainable; a joint degree of Wageningen University and Breda University of Applied Sciences.
programmes.overview: Year one covers tourism, sociology, economics, environmental sciences and research methods, ending in a National Field Practicum in the Netherlands. Year two adds development, intercultural studies, landscape planning and environmental systems analysis, with tourism simulations and an international field practicum. Teaching is lectures and problem-based tutorials in which a group and a supervisor solve a case. Year three offers electives, then specialisations such as risk communication or community development, and a bachelor's thesis. The degree is taught jointly with Breda University of Applied Sciences, and graduates work as junior strategists, marketers and researchers.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply early and send your marks so WUR can list any missing subjects. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: WUR's 2027 deadlines are not yet published; for 2026 entry EU/EEA applicants applied in Studielink by 15 June (non-EU by 15 April).
Send a recent list of marks early: WUR assesses you on it and its result letter says which subject conditions you must still meet.
Its other twelve bachelor's, including Biology and Plant Sciences, are Dutch-taught and need proof of Dutch as well as English.
